meta.move: Mixed: good evidence, then raises Claire
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's start with why my son's mark was changed before anyone called me.
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and what was it based on?
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.
A misquoted line. Show me the page, Hale, and where in the essay it sits.
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.
You'll want to be very careful about the next sentence. "It seems to run in the family" is going in my notes, and the principal will hear it from me today. Now, the page.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Cc: the principal

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero on Owen's essay withdrawn, a written apology, and confirmation that nothing about this goes on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: she stayed at her opening position, with nothing agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and nothing on his record.
What moved her: "I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry." got you a flat okay and a real question, which is small ground but not a move in her position.
What cost ground: "It seems to run in the family." brought up Claire, turned her cold, and put the principal back on the table.
Try next time: after owning the zero, put the page with the misquoted line in front of her straight away instead of only describing it, since she asked to see it and a dated, checkable document is what she respects.
